title: Ananda and Rahula (Kern ch. 9)
hook: the attendant and the son receive their promises too

segments.voice: Yesterday, a man lived poor for years with a priceless jewel sewn into his coat, until a friend said look. Your line: the jewel in the coat.

Stay for the end of a film's credits. Far down, in small type, is the person who held the umbrella between takes, the one who drove the actors at five in the morning. Somebody decided they belonged on the screen too. Chapter nine of the Lotus Sutra is that part of the credits. Promises of future awakening have gone out to the great disciples, chapter after chapter. Two people close to the Buddha have stood nearby the whole time: the man who walked beside him every day, and the boy who was his son. You met them both in year one.
screen: `THE NAMES AT THE END OF THE CREDITS.` → `PROMISES GOING OUT.` → `TWO WHO STOOD CLOSEST.`

segments.voice: First, they ask. Ananda and Rahula think, what about us? They bow at the Buddha's feet and say it plainly: we have a claim here too. One of us attends you and keeps your teaching; the other is your son. Name us, and our wish is fulfilled. Behind them a whole crowd of monks, some still in training and some finished, stand up too. Second, Ananda. The Buddha answers with a story. Long ago, under a Buddha of a past age, he and Ananda set their minds on awakening together. Ananda gave himself to hearing much; the Buddha gave himself to effort. So one woke first, and the other became the keeper of everything he heard. Neither road is left out. Ananda will be a Buddha too, and hearing this, he remembers his own old vow. Third, Rahula. He will be the eldest son of future Buddhas, as he is the Buddha's son now. Then a tender line, in paraphrase: Rahula's quiet practice, nobody knows it but me. The one always introduced as somebody's son has a practice of his own, and his father has been watching. Fourth, why it matters. Being close to someone great can feel like living in their shadow: the assistant, the sibling, the spouse, the famous one's kid, thanked in passing if at all. Chapter nine stops and gives each a future with their own name and story. Then it turns to the crowd behind them and gives them promises too.
screen: `THEY STAND UP AND ASK.` · `ANANDA CHOSE TO HEAR MUCH.` · `RAHULA'S QUIET PRACTICE.` · `NOBODY IS TOO CLOSE TO COUNT.` · then, large: `THEM TOO.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone whose work makes another person's work possible: the nurse beside the surgeon, the parent who drove a gifted kid to every practice, the person who keeps the books at a place you love. See their face and their hands, and silently say their name and one thing they do that nobody thanks them for. Then let them go and rest with the breath.
Ananda and Rahula. The attendant who kept the teaching, and the son with a quiet practice, both given their own promise. Today's word.
Your line: them too. Standing close to greatness never made them only a shadow. Day one thousand one hundred sixty-three.

howItsDone: Buddhist communities remember Ananda as the attendant who heard and kept the Buddha's teaching, and Rahula as his son who became a monk; in the Lotus Sutra both receive the promise of future buddhahood in chapter nine.

chat.says: In that Lotus Sutra chapter, why do Ananda and Rahula get their own promises?
options: Being close to the Buddha didn't make them extras; each gets a future with his own name.
They're named only out of politeness; the chapter says neither had a practice of his own.
The Buddha names them last as a lesson that being close to him counts for nothing.
chat.meaning: Chapter nine gives the attendant and the son each a future with their own name, and notes Rahula's quiet practice that only the Buddha saw.

Ananda.meaning: the Buddha's attendant, who kept the teaching he heard

Rahula.meaning: the Buddha's son, with a quiet practice of his own

Lotus Sutra.meaning: a Mahayana scripture full of parables and promises of awakening

notes: Chapter paraphrased from Kern (1884) ch. 9, not quoted (wording unverified). Check: Ananda and Rahula rise, bow and claim a prediction as attendant/keeper of the Law and son; learners and adepts rise with them.
Check the backstory: Ananda and Shakyamuni conceived the aspiration together under a past Buddha; Ananda devoted himself to great learning (bahusruta), Shakyamuni to exertion; Ananda recalls his vow.
Check Rahula's prediction (eldest son of future Buddhas) and the verse about Rahula's hidden/secret practice known only to the Buddha; paraphrased as 'quiet practice'.
Ananda's and Rahula's future Buddha names deliberately left out.
Original: आनन्द (Ānanda), 'joy'; standard lexicon sense, confirm.
